messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: updated GitHub wiki for Dev Process and Dev Transition Process
parts:
I finished organizing and reformatting the Wiki instructions
on how to work with Stan's development process. It'd be great
if Daniel and/or Ben could check it for accuracy.

I removed the injunctions against pushing to hotfix or release
branches. My understanding is that these are just like
feature branches and we will work on them jointly, then like
for feature branches, an admin will merge them back to where
they belong.

I took the "how to transition" section from Daniel's notes and
made it its own page.

I simplified the pull request instructions to just one option.

I reduced the working in a fork instructions to just indicate what's
different from working in a clone. (The doc was too confusing to
scroll through otherwise.)

- Bob

On Sunday, May 19, 2013 8:43:04 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I removed the injunctions against pushing to hotfix or release
branches.  My understanding is that these are just like
feature branches and we will work on them jointly, then like
for feature branches, an admin will merge them back to where
they belong.

If you want people to be able to push into hotfix or release branches, then you need to change the link to the pre-push hook back to the old one (which only blocks pushing to master and development at origin). But it doesn't seem consistent to me to require a pull request to push into the develop branch but no pull request is needed to push into something (hotfix or release) that could be merged into master at any millisecond.

Ben

I don't have particularly strong opinions one way or another.
I just didn't understand how we'd work without pushing into
hotfix or release.

If we don't have push permission for hotfix or release, how do
more than one of us work on a hotfix or a release branch?

I thought we'd just handle them like features and set them up to
be writable and then use pull requests to test them and finally
have an admin merge them back into develop and/or master.

How were you thinking this would go?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: updated GitHub wiki for Dev Process and Dev Transition Process
parts:
On Monday, May 20, 2013 2:37:37 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
If we don't have push permission for hotfix or release, how do
more than one of us work on a hotfix or a release branch?

For a release branch, I had assumed it would just be you and Daniel working on it, and you two can push to it. The commits to a release branch should be largely administrative (bumping version numbers and stuff) But you have a big problem if I decide to push a bug into a release branch one second before you push it into master.

For a hotfix branch, it could exist publicly with some other name (if it is so hard that it requires multiple people to fix) and then on a pull request get renamed to hotfix-* and pushed into master and develop. But a hotfix branch is usually going to be approximately one commit, so I doubt there would be much collaboration on it anyway.

Ben

We have the same problem if we push a bug into the release branch

I'm hoping we can communicate so that doesn't happen on release branches.
